title: Charles Schwab website briefly goes down as brokerage becomes latest financial service to encounter issues
excerpt: Charles Schwab's website briefly went down on Tuesday, displaying an error code before coming back online around 10:38 a.m. ET.
content_html:
By Natalie Musumeci

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-17T18:26:22.819Z

The brokerage giant Charles Schwab is the latest financial service to run into issues this week.

Charles Schwab's website briefly went down for some users on Tuesday. The site temporarily displayed a message saying its server "encountered an internal error or misconfiguration and was unable to complete your request."

The website was working properly again around 10:38 a.m. ET.

A spokesperson for Charles Schwab told Business Insider that a "brief webpage loading issue has been resolved."

"Trading remained available, and clients could access their accounts at schwab.com/login or through the Schwab Mobile app. We apologize for the inconvenience," the spokesperson added.

Earlier Tuesday, outage reports for the financial services company spiked on the third-party website DownDetector.com. By 10:20 a.m. ET, there were more than 1,400 reports of disruptions.

The website issue follows a recent spate of widespread outages that hit major banks, disrupted Microsoft services, and led to a nationwide ground stop, causing thousands of flight delays and cancellations.

Correction, November 17, 2026 — Charles Schwab's website experienced issues on Tuesday, not Monday.

Natalie is a senior reporter on Business Insider's Business News team covering the AI and data center boom.She was previously on BI's Legal Affairs team, where she handled major cases coming out of state and federal court, as well as bankruptcy. Her coverage often focused on stories at the intersection of law, business, politics, and technology. Natalie has covered Donald Trump’s criminal and civil cases, the wave of lawsuits against the second Trump administration, the indictment and criminal trial of Sean “Diddy” Combs, the shooting death of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, and the legal battles facing Elon Musk and his companies. Natalie came to Business Insider in June 2021 as a breaking news reporter, focusing on the most interesting angles on the day's trending news. Natalie largely drove BI’s coverage around the fatal “Rust” shooting involving Alec Baldwin and the disappearance and murder of Gabby Petito.Prior to joining BI, Natalie worked for the New York Post, the New York Daily News, and The Brooklyn Paper. She has an extensive background covering crime and courts. During her more than 12-year journalism career, she did a stint covering the police beat out of the New York Police Department's headquarters. Natalie, a Brooklyn native, graduated from Brooklyn College in 2012 with a degree in journalism.
